EXCEPT FOR CLAIMS UNDER SECTION 9 HEREOF, THE LIABILITY OF A PARTY TO THE OTHER FOR DIRECT DAMAGES SHALL NOT EXCEED FIFTEEN MILLION DOLLARS.
findings.explanation: Section 10 caps direct damages at fifteen million dollars but explicitly excludes claims under Section 9 (Indemnification) from this cap. This means my liability for indemnification claims is completely uncapped and exposes me to disproportionate financial risk.
findings.suggested_change: Propose capping all liability, including indemnification claims, under the mutual fifteen million dollar cap or a reasonable aggregate liability cap.

findings.quoted_text: Upon the effective date of the termination, all outstanding invoices and other invoicable amounts will become due and payable. Co-Host's contractual right to the marketing consideration shall cease immediately upon the effective date of the termination. Termination or expiration of this Agreement if by reason of material breach by Co-Host shall not affect any of Co-Host's payment obligations, all of which survive termination of this Agreement...
findings.explanation: Upon termination for my alleged breach, I immediately lose all marketing rights and access that I paid millions for, while my obligation to pay remaining fees or invoices survives indefinitely. This creates a one-sided penalty where NAI retains payments and marketing control without providing consideration.
findings.suggested_change: Ensure that upon termination by NAI without cause or due to NAI breach, pre-paid fees are refunded on a pro-rata basis, and survival of payment obligations is restricted to services already satisfactorily rendered or products delivered.

findings.quoted_text: Late payments shall bear interest at the lesser of: (i) the maximum rate permitted by law, and (ii) the rate of 1.5% per month from the due date until paid.
findings.explanation: A late payment interest rate of 1.5% per month amounts to an annualized rate of 18%, which is excessively punitive and unfavorable.
findings.suggested_change: Reduce the late payment interest rate to a commercially reasonable rate, such as 1% per month (12% per annum), applicable only after a reasonable cure period and written notice.

findings.quoted_text: Co-Host will provide to NAI on Monday of each week, a computer media data file in the format established by NAI showing Co-Host's current inventory levels of each Product (including items in transit), and weekly runrate snapshots and the other information reasonably requested by NAI.
findings.explanation: The inclusion of other information reasonably requested by NAI creates open-ended reporting obligations that can expand administrative burdens and introduce scope creep beyond the agreed-upon weekly inventory and sales reports.
findings.suggested_change: Remove the open-ended request for other information reasonably requested and limit reporting obligations strictly to the standard sales-out and inventory files explicitly defined in the contract.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello. Thank you for sharing the agreement. I have reviewed the terms and would like to propose a few adjustments before signing: - Regarding the relevant clause on liability, the current terms leave indemnification claims uncapped, creating disproportionate financial risk. I propose applying a reasonable aggregate liability cap to all claims. - In the relevant clause concerning late payments, the specified interest rate is excessively punitive. I suggest reducing this to a standard commercial rate that applies after a reasonable cure period. - Regarding the reporting obligations in the agreement, the open-ended request for additional information creates unnecessary administrative burdens. I propose limiting reporting strictly to the standard inventory files explicitly defined in the contract. Thank you for your flexibility, and I look forward to finalizing this.
